beats.role_note: Open the weekly update and establish the Learn - Contribute - Build progression.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Akshay, for Humanitarians AI. This week I focused on reviewing and approving Claude Bear videos, continuing to study Professor Brown's Brutalist video style, and building a new technical explainer about Redis.
beats.visual_intent: Simple opener. Show WEEKLY UPDATE and the three-part progression: LEARN, CONTRIBUTE, BUILD. Keep the frame clean.

props.command: Summarize this week's progress at Humanitarians AI.

beats.role_note: Explain learning the Brutalist production workflow.
beats.narration_text: I reviewed fourteen videos from the Claude Bear folder, checking the content before publication and making sure each video was ready for the Humanitarians AI YouTube channel.
beats.visual_intent: Minimal process graphic. Four simple labels appear in sequence: SCRIPT, AUDIO, VISUALS, QC. No dense arrows or flowchart.

beats.role_note: Show the scale and type of Claude Bear content reviewed and uploaded.
beats.narration_text: After reviewing them, I approved all fourteen videos for the Claude Basics playlist on the Humanitarians AI YouTube channel, continuing my work supporting the project's content review and publishing pipeline.
beats.visual_intent: Large 14 VIDEOS number with a small restrained grid of representative titles. Do not show all fourteen titles at once and do not use a complex diagram.

beats.role_note: Show that reviewed videos were organized into the appropriate Humanitarians AI playlists.
beats.narration_text: I also spent more time watching Professor Brown's Brutalist videos. I focused on the typography, pacing, visual hierarchy, scene composition, and motion so I can apply those conventions more consistently.
beats.visual_intent: Two simple playlist cards: CLAUDE BASICS and EXTENDING CLAUDE, with a few video cards moving into them. Maximum two destination boxes.

beats.role_note: Show the Kafka explainer as the week's build milestone.
beats.narration_text: Finally, I created a new technical explainer called How Redis Handles Millions of Requests. I used the Brutalist production workflow to build technical visuals and narration explaining how Redis processes large numbers of requests efficiently.
beats.visual_intent: Show the Kafka explainer title, then two clean format cards: 16:9 4K and 9:16 4K. Kafka concepts appear as a short text list, not a network diagram.

props.artifactHeading: How Redis Handles Millions of Requests

beats.role_note: Close on the week's progression and Humanitarians AI identity.
beats.narration_text: So this week was about reviewing and approving content, continuing to study the Brutalist visual language, and applying it by building another technical explainer. I'm Akshay Chavan, for Humanitarians AI.
beats.visual_intent: Clean three-word recap: LEARN. CONTRIBUTE. BUILD. Then branded Humanitarians AI sign-off.
